title: Will you get struck by lightning? (people who were, and lived)

lines: This man got struck by lightning seven times. And lived.
Roy Sullivan, park ranger. Strike one, in 1942, burned a strip down his leg and blew a hole in his shoe.
How did he live? Speed. A bolt is over in millionths of a second, so most current skims over the skin and out through the feet.
Strike two came through his truck window and took his eyebrows. Windows up, a car's metal shell carries current around you.
After that, his hair caught fire so often, he kept a can of water handy.
Golfer Lee Trevino got hit too. His joke? Hold up a 1-iron. Not even God can hit a 1-iron.
Some people get fern-shaped marks called Lichtenberg figures. They fade within hours.
What kills is a stopped heart, so CPR saves lives.
Your odds? About one in a million a year, and nine in ten survive.
So why Roy? Pure luck would be one in ten to the thirty-three. He just spent decades outdoors in storm country.
Strike seven hit him fishing. Hair smoking, he says he then fought off a bear trying to steal his trout. With a stick.
Would you go fishing with Roy? When thunder roars, go indoors.
